# EmptyState

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

media and display · tier 1 · beta · renders on the server and ships no client JavaScript.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

What a list, a table or a search renders when it has nothing to show. With no props it
shows the tray icon and the two `labels.state` strings. Pass a `title` and the default
description goes too, because it would describe the wrong thing.

```tsx
<EmptyState title="No projects yet" description="Create your first project and it will show up here.">
  <Button size="sm" render={<a href="/projects/new" />}>New project</Button>
</EmptyState>
```

It has no role and no live region: it is page content, read in place. `null` hides the
icon, the title or the description, and the action is always the caller's own Button.

<!-- /hand-written -->

## Import

```tsx
import { EmptyState } from 'topclassui'
```

## Props

Every prop below is optional and falls back to the default shown.

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | no | `ReactNode` | - | The action, which the caller passes as a Button. The component draws none of its own. |
| `description` | no | `ReactNode` | - | Defaults to `labels.state.emptyDescription` only while `title` is unset too; `null` hides it. |
| `icon` | no | `ReactNode` | - | Above the title. Defaults to the tray icon in the muted colour; `null` hides it. |
| `labels` | no | `Labels` | - | The built-in strings. Defaults to English; pass `getLabels(locale).labels` for another. |
| `locale` | no | `string` | - | Accepted so `{...getLabels(locale)}` spreads cleanly. Nothing here formats a number, so it is not used and never reaches the element. |
| `title` | no | `ReactNode` | - | The bold first line, a paragraph and not a heading. Defaults to `labels.state.empty`; `null` hides it. |

Anything else is passed to the root element, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
